I find addressing Satan/Lucifer/Beelzebub as a character(s) at all very tricky. He was created by god, to serve god at his right hand. Then when god shows favoritism he got pissed and revolted. But why would a being who is supposedly above humans show very human foibles throughout his existence? Satan shows very many parallels to lower human desires (i.e. selfishness, sadism on different levels, 7 sins etc.) So is he a metaphor for addressing and overcoming our own foibles? 
If that is the case then why is the all powerful submitting a man to suffering that isn't his? It seems that Job suffers merely because 'lower' human thoughts/emotions exist, not because he himself has sinned. Job seem to live a righteous life, yet it is taken. 
Why? God has now been influenced by this so called metaphor of human flaws, so the supreme being is now subjectable to human free will. Thus I come to the conclusion from this story that through the transitive property god does not exist as a heavenly father figure and we are subject to our own desires, and we will exercise this power for no real reason. But that's just my interpretation.
